title: Betaine - Impryl USA
abstract:
### Introduction  
Found in everything from turkey to shrimp, beef to brown rice, betaine has long been studied within the athletic community based on its ability to enhance body composition and performance. Being a source of methyl groups, betaine helps prevent the build-up of homocysteine, an amino acid linked to heart and circulation problems, skeletal complications, and potential fertility issues.
### What Is Betaine?  
While betaine is produced in the body, it is also found in plants, animals, and microorganisms.  
Betaine is an amino acid that was first discovered in the juice of sugar beets. Shown to help fight against heart complications, build muscle mass, and improve body composition, betaine promotes protein synthesis. Not only does betaine help metabolize homocysteine, but it’s also involved in liver function, cellular reproduction, and helps make carnitine, an amino acid involved in energy production.  
Also known as trimethylglycine, betaine is a derivative of choline. This means that choline must be present for betaine synthesis to occur. Betaine also functions closely with folic acid and vitamin B12. Composed of the amino acid glycine, which is attached to three methyl groups, betaine has two major functions:  
- It acts as a methyl donor and is a critical component of various physiological processes. In this case, it helps convert harmful levels of homocysteine into methionine.
- It acts as an osmolyte, creating fluid balance inside and outside cells. That is why betaine is often found in high concentrations in plants facing drought.
### How Betaine Affects Fertility  
Since high homocysteine levels can have a negative impact on both male and female fertility, it’s important to address even moderately high levels. Betaine’s ability to decrease plasma homocysteine in human adults has been published in multiple journals. One study found that supplementing with betaine for six weeks lowered homocysteine levels.1 Lower levels of homocysteine support a more optimal reproductive process, particularly in relation to sperm concentrations, oocyte quality, and overall fertility.  
Betaine has also been specifically studied in relation to male fertility, focusing on betaine’s role as a potentially useful tool for improving reproductive traits in response to stress. After all, stress plays a key role in both sperm function and motility, as well as cell quality and overall fertility. Studied in roosters, it was found that betaine may increase semen quality, fertility, and welfare of breeder males exposed to chronic heat stress.2 Similar results were shown in another study, as betaine supplementation reduced homocysteine concentration in boars while increasing sperm production.3
